bib.venue: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026 (arXiv:2510.04618v3, 29 Mar 2026)

question: How can an LLM's input context be adapted over time, offline or online, without losing detail to brevity bias or context collapse?
hypothesis: Contexts should act as comprehensive, evolving playbooks updated by small incremental deltas rather than rewritten as concise summaries, and this will beat prompt optimizers and monolithic-rewrite memory methods.
contributions: ACE: a Generator, Reflector, Curator framework that treats context as an evolving playbook of itemized bullets
Incremental delta updates merged by non-LLM logic, plus a grow-and-refine step (dedup by embeddings, lazy or proactive pruning)
Gains of 10.6% on agents and 8.6% on domain-specific benchmarks over strong baselines, with and without ground-truth labels
Lower adaptation latency, rollouts and token cost than GEPA and Dynamic Cheatsheet

method.summary: ACE keeps context as a playbook of bullets (id, helpful/harmful counters, content). A Generator produces trajectories and marks which bullets helped, a Reflector (up to 5 refinement rounds) distills lessons, and a Curator emits ADD delta operations that are merged deterministically into the playbook; embedding dedup and pruning keep it compact. Evaluated offline (optimize on train split, test on test) and online (predict, then update, sequentially on shuffled test split) against ICL, MIPROv2, GEPA and Dynamic Cheatsheet, mostly with DeepSeek-V3.1 as every role.
method.task: context adaptation (system prompt optimisation and test-time agent memory) on agent tasks (AppWorld) and domain reasoning (FiNER, Formula, DDXPlus, BIRD-SQL)

No seeds, repeats or significance tests reported. IBM CUGA is a rough contextual reference only, not a baseline.

limits: Authors concede ACE relies on a reasonably strong Reflector; with no reliable feedback (no GT labels or execution signal) both ACE and DC can degrade below the base model (Table 2).
Not all tasks need rich contexts: HotPotQA and Game of 24 benefit from concise instructions.
No seeds, repeats, variance or significance tests are reported; decoding temperature and max tokens are not stated.
Headline numbers use one backbone (DeepSeek-V3.1) with the same model in all roles; gains on Llama-3.3-70B are small (+1.1 to +2.4).
Longer contexts cost more raw input tokens at evaluation (+117.4% vs GEPA); the cost claim depends on KV/prompt caching.
IBM CUGA is only a rough contextual reference; authors disclaim direct comparison.
Context collapse is demonstrated in a single case study (one run, via Dynamic Cheatsheet), not measured across runs.
Table 18 and Table 19 give different test-normal averages (70.3 vs 67.6) for what appears to be the same 5-round offline setup.
Leaderboard snapshot dated 09/2025 and has likely dated.

terms.definition: methods that improve model behavior by constructing or modifying inputs to an LLM, rather than altering its weights
the tendency of optimization to collapse toward short, generic prompts
arises when an LLM is tasked with fully rewriting the accumulated context at each adaptation step; the model compresses it into much shorter, less informative summaries
context as a collection of structured, itemized bullets (metadata with id and helpful/harmful counters, plus content) that accumulates strategies
bullets with new identifiers are appended, existing bullets updated in place, then a de-duplication step prunes redundancy by comparing bullets via semantic embeddings, proactively or lazily

figures.caption: Context Collapse. Monolithic rewriting of context by an LLM can collapse it into shorter, less informative summaries, leading to sharp performance drops.

figures.caption: The ACE Framework. Inspired by Dynamic Cheatsheet, ACE adopts an agentic architecture with three specialized components: a Generator, a Reflector, and a Curator.
figures.why: Loop of query, trajectory, insights, delta context items merged into the playbook.

figures.caption: Cost and Speed Analysis. We measure the context adaptation latency, number of rollouts, and dollar costs of ACE against GEPA (offline) and DC (online).
